query_text: tips to avoid fake job scams

messages.content: tips to avoid fake job scams

message.content:
Here are practical ways to **avoid fake job scams**:

- **Verify the employer** before responding. Search the company name plus “scam,” “review,” or “complaint,” and check whether the role appears on the company’s official career page.[3][4][2]
- **Inspect the email/domain carefully.** Generic messages, misspellings, or email addresses that do not match the company’s domain are common red flags.[1][2][5]
- **Be skeptical of “too good to be true” offers.** Promises of high pay for little work, no experience, or instant hiring are common scam signs.[1][3][6]
- **Never pay to get a job.** Legitimate employers will not ask for application fees, training fees, equipment purchases, or “refundable” payments.[3][4][6]
- **Do not cash or forward checks.** Fake-check scams often ask you to deposit a check and send part of the money elsewhere; the check later bounces.[2][4]
- **Protect sensitive information.** Do not share bank account details, Social Security number, credit card info, or ID documents until you have verified the employer and are far enough into a legitimate hiring process.[2][5][6]
- **Watch for pressure tactics.** Scammers often rush you to decide quickly, avoid real interviews, or communicate only through messaging apps.[2][6]
- **Prefer real interviews.** Lack of an in-person or on-camera interview is a warning sign, especially if the “recruiter” avoids direct contact.[1][2][6]
- **Ask someone you trust.** Describing the offer to another person can help you spot inconsistencies and avoid rushing into a scam.[3][4]
- **Check the recruiter’s identity.** Look up the recruiter on LinkedIn and compare their details with the company’s website and email format.[5][2]

If you want, I can also give you a **quick scam-check checklist** you can use on any job posting or recruiter message.
